theme: Alan and Bridgette plumb the deep sea from the comfort of their couch

events.text: Okay, put your phone down, I'm about to change your whole evening.
Is it a documentary? Please say it's a deep-ocean documentary.
It's a deep-ocean documentary.
Bridgette. We've been together three years. I've never been more attracted to you than right now.
The Mariana Trench goes down almost eleven kilometres. If you dropped Mount Everest in it, the peak would still be over two kilometres underwater.
So you're telling me we have an entire Everest sitting down there just... waiting, like a dog nobody walks.
Okay, but here's my thing. We spent all week complaining we can't afford a one-bedroom in this city, and there's a fish down there literally growing its own lamp.
The anglerfish. The little lure dangles off its head and glows.
It glows? Like a tiny headlamp.
Bacteria living inside it make the light. The fish just rents the glow.
So even the deep-sea fish is subletting. That's so Toronto.
And the males? Some of them bite onto the female and just... fuse. Become part of her, permanently.
Okay so my strategy of attaching myself to you and never getting a real job is officially scientifically valid.
You've been reading the Wikipedia tab at 2 a.m. again, haven't you?
So what's the actual point of your deep-sea binge, you're not quitting your job to be an anglerfish.
No, but listen — most of the ocean's deep zones have never been mapped in detail. We've got better maps of Mars than of our own seafloor.
That's the most 'you' fact I've heard all week. Mars gets a nicer map than Lake Ontario.
It's the same instinct. You look at the dark and you want to know what's in it.
And what's in it, according to you, is a fish with a face like a porch light.
The anglerfish, yeah. The little lure glows because of bacteria living inside it. Bioluminescence. A whole roommate situation.
So it's not even its own light. It's subletting the glow. In this economy?
And the weird part is, we've only mapped a small fraction of the ocean floor in high detail. There's more ocean than there is land, and most of it we've just... glanced at.
So we're sitting on a planet that's mostly a mystery, and we named the moon better than we named the deep.
They call it the hadal zone. Like Hades. Because it's basically the underworld down there.
Great. So we live above a haunted basement and we still can't get rent under two thousand.
Different deep sea. Same pressure though.
Double-double and a box of Timbits, we're fueling this expedition properly.
I feel like the anglerfish would absolutely order a double-double. Whole camouflage, then a light appears.
And the light is just a tiny Timbit on a fishing line.
Okay that's genuinely how it works, the lure is a modified fin with glowing bacteria living on it. Symbiosis. The bacteria glow, the fish gets dinner.
So it's a partnership. One glows, the other eats. That's just us, but with more teeth.
